payload.title: Moving magnet and resistive coil: illustrative dipole approximation

model.title: Moving magnet and resistive coil: illustrative dipole approximation
model.description: Unqualified teaching proposal for human review. An axial magnetic dipole moves through a stationary circular coil. Normalized flux linkage F=p/(1+(x/a)^2)^(3/2); actual linkage is F times 0.0001 V s. Faraday voltage is minus its time derivative. Positive current circulates counterclockwise viewed from +x and produces a +x coil field. time_experiment: input=time; step_seconds=0.02; playback_speed=1; reset_on_change=[initial_position,speed,pole_orientation,circuit_closed]; end=
assumptions: All defaults and ranges are illustrative teaching assumptions, not learner settings or product specifications.
The coil centre is x=0; +x points along its axis. Its fixed radius is 0.05 m and it has 100 identical closely spaced turns.
The magnet is represented electromagnetically by an ideal point dipole. Its schematic north and south markers are separated by 0.01 m; these are not measured dimensions.
The standard axial-dipole/circular-loop flux integral gives linkage proportional to (a²+x²)^(-3/2). This is an approximation for a compact bar magnet, not an invented field law.
The chosen peak flux linkage is 0.0001 V s. The voltage reference is this linkage divided by the fixed 1 s reference time.
pole_orientation=+1 means the dipole moment points +x, with north at the higher-x marker; -1 reverses it.
Magnet motion is externally prescribed: x=initial_position+speed*time. Initial position is set at time zero; speed remains constant during each run.
The circuit has a fixed total resistance of 100 ohm. Closed-circuit current is voltage/resistance; open-circuit conduction current is zero while induced voltage remains.
Assume total inductance no greater than 0.001 H, giving L/R no greater than 0.00001 s, much shorter than the minimum 1 s spatial-variation timescale. Ignore switching and startup boundary layers.
Time runs from 0 to 3 s and stops at 3 s. Changing any other input restarts time atomically; pausing remains under learner control.
Provide comparisons at the same position using opposite speeds, different speed magnitudes, and zero speed. Changing pole orientation reverses flux and voltage signs.
All positive-current arrows, voltage-polarity indicators and coil-field explanations must use the same signed voltage/current state.
limitations: No detailed bar-magnet field map, microscopic charge dynamics, distributed winding geometry, circuit capacitance or coil-inductance transients.
No quantitative magnetic force, mechanical work, magnet deceleration, magnetic materials, hysteresis or energy-loss prediction.
Lenz's law and the external mechanical work needed against magnetic reaction are explained qualitatively; no force calculation is supplied.
The instantaneous resistive approximation does not resolve opening/closing transients. Moving circuit charges are represented by signed current, not calculated carrier drift speed.
Normalized flux linkage is dimensionless because the available unit vocabulary lacks magnetic-flux units; its fixed physical reference is explicitly stated.
This is a finite constant-speed teaching run, not a general motion or electromagnetic solver.

definition.title: Moving magnet and coil
definition.description: A simplified teaching apparatus connects magnet motion to changing flux, induced voltage and current in a closed circuit.

parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Default 0 s; range [0,3] s. Constant-speed motion starts at the initial position.

parts.label: Magnet position
parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Dipole centre coordinate; bounded within ±0.30 m.

parts.explanation: Schematic readout overview. Default +0.025 m/s; range [-0.05,0.05] m/s. Zero holds the magnet stationary.

limits: All construction dimensions, defaults and supported ranges are illustrative teaching assumptions, not measured specifications.
Common mapping: 100 scene units per metre on every axis; equations retain SI values. Circuit components and supports have illustrative dimensions.
The stationary coil has radius 0.05 m and 100 turns. The magnet is electromagnetically an ideal point dipole; its illustrative pole markers are separated by 0.01 m.

Initial position ranges from -0.15 to +0.15 m, default -0.10 m; signed speed ranges from -0.05 to +0.05 m/s, default +0.025 m/s. Pole orientation is -1 or +1, default +1; circuit closure is 0 or 1, default 1.

Magnet centre positions span -0.30 to +0.30 m. Time runs from 0 to 3 s and stops at 3 s; changing another input resets time atomically. Preserve mobile, keyboard, reduced-motion, pause and inspection controls; inactivity never resumes playback.
Flux linkage follows the accepted axial-dipole/circular-loop approximation, with normalized linkage referenced to 0.0001 V s. Visible winding thickness does not change the equations.

Total resistance is 100 ohm. Assumed inductance at most 0.001 H gives L/R at most 0.00001 s, much shorter than the minimum 1 s spatial-variation timescale. Startup and switching boundary layers are omitted.

Opening the circuit removes conduction current, not induced voltage. Positive current is counterclockwise viewed from +x and produces a +x coil field. Signed current and polarity indicators must follow the same accepted state, without implying calculated carrier drift speeds or instrument loading. Additional current readouts are deferred from this compact layout stage, not excluded from the later

parts.label: Apparatus base
parts.explanation: The base holds the coil and circuit still while the magnet moves.

parts.label: Coil supports
parts.explanation: These insulating feet hold the coil above the base. They leave its middle open for the magnet.

parts.label: Hollow coil spool
parts.explanation: This hollow spool supports the wire loops. The magnet passes through its open middle.

parts.label: 100 copper turns
parts.explanation: These wire loops form the coil. Changing magnetic flux through them induces voltage.

parts.label: Moving bar magnet
parts.explanation: This magnet moves along the coil's axis, the line through its centre. The speed control sets its motion.

parts.label: North pole
parts.explanation: N marks the magnet's north end. Reversing the pole setting swaps the ends.

parts.label: South pole
parts.explanation: S marks the south end. It stays opposite the north marker.

parts.label: Coil terminal A
parts.explanation: This terminal joins one coil end to the return circuit. A terminal is a place where wires connect.

parts.label: Coil terminal B
parts.explanation: This terminal joins the other coil end to the circuit. Both connections are needed for a complete loop.

parts.label: Connecting wires
parts.explanation: These wires connect the coil, resistor and switch. Current needs an unbroken return path.

parts.label: Resistive return path
parts.explanation: This resistor represents resistance in the return path. The whole circuit, including the coil, has 100 ohms of resistance.

parts.label: Switch contacts and guide
parts.explanation: These separated contacts leave a gap in the circuit. The guide holds a sliding bridge over them.

parts.label: Sliding switch bridge
parts.explanation: This metal bridge joins the contacts when closed. Moving it aside breaks the current path.

parts.label: Signed state display
parts.explanation: This panel reports flux, voltage and current. Positive coil current runs counterclockwise when viewed from +x.

parts.label: Axial position scale
parts.explanation: This scale shows the magnet's position along x. Zero marks the coil's centre.

experiments.title: Approach versus withdrawal
experiments.prompt: At time zero and initial position -0.10 m, predict the voltage sign when speed changes from +0.025 to -0.025 m/s. Then play.
experiments.explanation: The magnet reverses motion. At equal position and pole orientation, linkage is unchanged but its rate and induced voltage reverse signs.

experiments.title: Move faster
experiments.prompt: Compare speeds +0.025 and +0.05 m/s at time zero, with initial position -0.10 m. Predict the voltage magnitude.
experiments.explanation: At equal position, doubling speed doubles the linkage-change rate and induced voltage. Closed-circuit current follows voltage through the fixed 100-ohm resistance.

experiments.title: Stop the magnet
experiments.prompt: At initial position -0.10 m, predict whether stopping removes flux linkage or its rate of change. Set speed to zero.
experiments.explanation: The stationary magnet retains flux linkage, but linkage no longer changes. Induced voltage and conduction current are zero in this model.

experiments.title: Swap the poles
experiments.prompt: Restore speed +0.025 m/s and initial position -0.10 m. At time zero, predict how reversing pole orientation changes voltage.
experiments.explanation: The north and south markers swap ends. At equal position and speed, reversing the dipole reverses linkage, its rate of change and induced voltage.

controls.help: Sets the magnet's starting position and restarts time. All defaults and ranges are illustrative teaching assumptions.
Sets constant signed magnet speed and restarts time. Zero holds it still; reversing speed reverses voltage at equal position.
Swaps north and south and restarts time. At equal position and speed, linkage and induced voltage reverse signs.
Moves the switch bridge and restarts time. Opening removes conduction current without removing motion-induced voltage.
Advances prescribed constant-speed motion from the starting position. Playback stops at 3 seconds.

time_experiment.explanation: From time zero, position equals initial position plus speed times time. The dipole-loop linkage gives Faraday voltage through its analytic derivative. Runs stop at 3 s; parameter changes reset time atomically without resuming paused playback. Current uses the stated negligible-inductance resistive approximation.

coverage.explanation: Prescribed motion changes dipole-loop linkage; its negative time derivative gives voltage. The model computes closed-circuit current as voltage divided by 100 ohms, or zero when open. Current is not an additional displayed readout in this saved layout.

At equal position, reversing speed reverses voltage, increasing speed scales its magnitude, and stopping gives zero linkage-change rate and voltage. Closed-circuit current follows voltage through fixed resistance.

Inspect the coil and return path. Positive current is counterclockwise viewed from +x and produces a +x coil field. Lenz's law describes opposition to flux change, not necessarily existing flux. Magnetic reaction and external mechanical work remain qualitative. Forces, microscopic charge dynamics, detailed fields and inductive transients are not resolved. Inspection separation is not physical motion.

outcomes: Connect relative magnet motion to changing magnetic flux through the coil, induced voltage, and current in a closed circuit.
Explore how motion speed and direction affect induced current, including what happens when the magnet stops.
Understand how the induced current's magnetic effect opposes the change in flux, consistent with Lenz's law.

sampled_quality.scope: Defaults, five points per input plus presets, a midpoint context for apparently inactive controls, all-input endpoints, and lesson experiments. Finite geometry and observed changes only; no proof of scientific accuracy, recognizability or complete state-space coverage.
